items.description: App renders the FileStock page when navigated to the filing route via MemoryRouter initialEntries pointing at that path
The SKU input on the FileStock page carries its data-testid seam
The location input on the FileStock page carries its data-testid seam
The quantity input on the FileStock page carries its data-testid seam
The inventory_code input on the FileStock page carries its data-testid seam
The submit button on the FileStock page carries its data-testid seam
The boundary layer (app/routes/) contains no import of the database session at any scope
The service layer (app/services/) contains no import of any ORM class or database session
The application reads its database connection string exclusively from the DATABASE_URL environment variable with no hardcoded connection string present in the codebase
The Alembic migration for stock_records completes a full downgrade-then-upgrade cycle on the real branch without error (marked @pytest.mark.migration, never downgrades past base)
POSTing a new stock record with a uuid-suffixed SKU and location to the JSON API returns a success response that includes the submitted SKU, location, quantity, and inventory_code
Inserting a stock_record row that violates the NOT NULL constraint on any required column is rejected by the real branch database
A direct insert of a stock_record row with quantity less than zero is rejected by the database CHECK constraint on the real branch
The service layer rejects a stock write whose resulting quantity would be negative before the repository layer is reached
A validation failure response from the boundary layer identifies the specific field that failed validation by name in the response body
App renders the stock retrieval page when navigated to the retrieval route via MemoryRouter initialEntries pointing at that path
The stock retrieval page displays the quantity value returned by the API
The stock retrieval page displays the inventory_code value returned by the API
The boundary layer (app/routes/) contains no server-side HTML template rendering calls
GETting a previously filed stock record from the JSON API returns a quantity and inventory_code that are byte-for-byte identical to the values that were POSTed
After filing stock for a SKU and location pair that already has a record, no error message element is present in the UI
POSTing a second stock record for an already-existing uuid-suffixed SKU and location pair via the JSON API returns a success response containing the updated quantity and inventory_code
Filing a stock record twice for the same (sku, location) pair results in exactly one row in stock_records on the real branch database

Two concurrent file operations for the same (sku, location) pair produce exactly one stored row in stock_records on the real branch database because the read-then-write executes within a single transaction
The created_at column value is unchanged after an in-place upsert updates an existing (sku, location) row on the real branch database
